headline: Every carton checked before it leaves the dock.
label: #FFFFFF
visitLine: Call and visit to one of your warehouses
heroLede: Mainfreight runs 337 branches in 27 countries, and its latest results point to warehousing getting more efficient as new sites fill up. Every carton that leaves a warehouse needs a sealed lid, the right shipping label and a barcode that scans. This is what a camera check could look like at the outbound end of a warehouse, as an example. We would match it to how your sites actually run. Scroll through, then adjust the estimate at the end to your own numbers.
lidLede: The camera checks every carton is taped shut, flaps down and not crushed. An open or damaged carton at the dock becomes a damage claim at the other end.
labelLede: A carton with another order’s label goes to the wrong city. The camera checks every carton carries the right shipping label for its order, straight and complete.
codeLede: A barcode that will not scan stops the carton at the next depot. The system reads the barcode on every carton and checks it matches the order it was packed for.
objectLede: Strapping, tape ends and loose packaging can end up on the conveyor. The camera over the belt spots anything that should not be there before it reaches the dock.

vocab.c1h: Taped shut, flaps down, not crushed
vocab.alert: Four cartons with loose tape in fifteen minutes. Check the taper.
